execution_boundaries: prior receipt, result digest, compact diagnosis, probe, ordinal, revision, and source snapshot validated before startup
one exact statically qualified target, test name, and browser project
owned or attested local Vite/Next runtime only
remote HTTP denied and caller cannot provide commands, paths, environment, base URLs, or network policy

real_product_evidence.interpretation: Both product surfaces executed the same closed probe and resolved the 12-versus-8 presentation gap. The next classification crossed the fixed CPU-ratio boundary in only one of two runs, demonstrating local variance and preventing a stable bottleneck or source-edit claim. The existing browser assertion failed in both runs.

limitations: Only the async/framework inventory-completion probe is executable in this version; other probe families remain inspection-only.
The operation runs a local development server and Playwright Chromium, so it consumes local CPU, memory, and wall time even though it makes no cloud or production call.
The owned Next runtime disables repository configuration and does not establish production-build equivalence.
Both High Signal assertions failed, so no optimization, correctness, or shipping claim is authorized.
The two new diagnoses selected different next probes around the 0.20 process-CPU ratio threshold, so repeated evidence is required before treating either route as stable.
